units.citation: Kimwanga et al. (2026). Who benefits from forest co-management? Heterogeneous welfare effects under rainfall shocks in Malawi. Trees, Forests and People.
units.quote:
Overall, the ATT results of the interaction between 
VNRMC participation and Rainfall shocks show that households 
participating in FCM through VNRMCs are have higher annual forestry 
income by 57% (Based on the difference of antilogs of 0.448 in Table 6), 
compared to non-participants. Conversely, VNRMC participation does 
not mitigate the effects of rainfall shocks’ on non-forestry income during 
the previous agricultural season. Despite the participation in VNRMC, 
the occurrence of rainfall shocks is likely to erode 36% of non-forestry 
income among smallholder households across forest reserves .
